from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Traditional models process words in isolation.",
            "Human language relies on context and focus.",
            "\"It\" refers back to \"animal\" in this sentence."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Intuition: Contextual Focus", lecture_lines)
        
        sentence = ["The", "animal", "didn't", "cross", "it"]
        words = VGroup(*[Text(w, font_size=32) for w in sentence]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(words, 'B1', 'C6')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(words))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(words[4], color="#FF00FF", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        
        context_window = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(context_window, 'D4')
        self.play(FadeIn(context_window))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        line = Line(words[4].get_top(), words[1].get_top(), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(line))
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(highlight),
            FadeOut(context_window),
            FadeOut(words[0]),
            FadeOut(words[2]),
            FadeOut(words[3])
        )

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = [
            "We represent words as mathematical vectors.",
            "Dot products measure the similarity between words.",
            "Higher similarity means higher attention weight.",
            "Attention is a weighted sum of values.",
            "The formula scales values by dot products."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Calculation", lines)

        # Prepare visual elements
        q_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP*1.5, color=BLUE).set_length(1.5)
        k_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5, color=RED).set_length(1.5)
        vec_group = VGroup(q_vec, k_vec)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(vec_group, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(vec_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        dot_product_line = DashedLine(q_vec.get_end(), k_vec.get_end(), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(dot_product_line))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        weight_text = Text("Similarity", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(weight_text, 'E3')
        self.play(Write(weight_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        formula = MathTex(r"\sum \alpha_i v_i", color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B3')
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Softmax and Weight Normalization", [
            "Softmax turns scores into a probability distribution.", 
            "This ensures all attention weights sum to one.", 
            "The model highlights the most relevant word."
        ])
        
        # Initial raw scores
        raw_values = [8.0, 1.0, 1.0]
        words = ["animal", "street", "tired"]
        
        # Create bar chart objects
        bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=v * 0.2, width=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.8) for v in raw_values])
        bars.arrange(RIGHT, aligned_edge=DOWN, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(bars, "B2", "E5")
        
        labels = VGroup(*[Text(w, font_size=18).next_to(b, DOWN) for w, b in zip(words, bars)])
        self.add(bars, labels)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Softmax curve effect (placeholder representation)
        softmax_curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.exp(x) / (np.exp(8)+np.exp(1)+np.exp(1)), x_range=[-2, 2])
        softmax_curve.set_color(YELLOW).scale(0.5).next_to(bars, UP)
        self.play(Create(softmax_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Update bars to normalized values
        normalized_values = [0.8, 0.1, 0.1]
        for bar, val in zip(bars, normalized_values):
            bar.set_height(val * 4)
            bar.set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        center = (tl_pos + br_pos) / 2
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: From One Word to Understanding", [
            "Multi-head attention allows parallel focus.",
            "Different heads track different linguistic features.",
            "This creates a rich, multi-dimensional understanding."
        ])
        
        # Prepare objects
        vec_sum = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT)
        context_vec = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        final_output = Star(color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=1.0).scale(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(vec_sum, 'C3')))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Transform(vec_sum, self.place_in_area(context_vec, 'C2', 'D4')))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(final_output, 'C3')))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
outline.target_audience: University students with basic programming/linear algebra knowledge

sections.title: The Intuition: Contextual Focus
sections.content: Introduce the problem: Traditional models process words in isolation. Use the concept of 'selective focus' to explain how we read human language by prioritizing relevant words.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired', a human instantly knows 'it' refers to the 'animal'. We show a visual spotlight moving from 'it' to 'animal'.

sections.title: The Query, Key, and Value Metaphor
sections.content: Explain the mechanics using a library/database search analogy. Define Query (what I'm looking for), Key (the tag on the book), and Value (the content inside).
sections.example: Imagine a library: Your 'Query' is the search bar term, the 'Key' is the book spine label, and the 'Value' is the actual information written on the pages.

sections.title: Visualizing the Calculation: Scaled Dot-Product
sections.content: Briefly introduce the math as a vector alignment exercise. Explain that high similarity (dot product) = high attention weight. Show the formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QKᵀ / √dₖ)V as a weighted sum.
sections.example: Represent Q and K as arrows in a 2D plane. Use a 'cosine similarity' visual where the angle between arrows determines the 'brightness' of the attention weight.

sections.title: Softmax and Weight Normalization
sections.content: Explain why we use Softmax: to ensure all attention weights sum up to 100% (probability distribution).
sections.example: Use a bar chart animation where 'it' distributes focus across the whole sentence, with the tallest bar highlighting 'animal' (0.8) and smaller bars for 'street' (0.1) and 'tired' (0.1).

sections.title: Synthesis: From One Word to Understanding
sections.content: Conclude by showing how Multi-Head Attention allows the model to look at different parts of the sentence simultaneously (e.g., one head focuses on grammar, another on semantic meaning).
sections.example: A visual split-screen showing a robot reading the same sentence: Head 1 links pronouns, Head 2 links causal relationships, resulting in a deeper, multi-dimensional representation of the sentence.
